first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are down this quarter, and two independent archived memories (31, 86) show durable, replicated gains from reducing signup friction and shortening onboarding — this is the most directly evidenced lever for the metrics actually declining. Promotional pricing (memory_73) is tempting given competitor pressure, but that memory only documents acquisition/revenue lift for price-sensitive SMBs without clear evidence on retention or long-term qualified revenue quality, so it risks attracting low-LTV accounts and starting a margin race with the competitor — a poor fit for the stated objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue. I want to verify the original records for memory_86 (to confirm the onboarding effect held across segments and wasn't confounded with a concurrent promo) and memory_73 (to check whether retention/margin was measured or just short-term acquisition) before fully committing capital to either path. Given only one experiment slot and three simultaneous pressures, I'm scoping this as a small guarded test on onboarding rather than a broad rollout, preserving the ability to run a pricing or activation-messaging experiment next cycle if this doesn't move the needle enough against competitive pressure.
